summary.headline: GSFC FY26 standalone sales rose 15% to INR10,827 crore and PAT 14% to INR652 crore; Q4 sales hit a record INR2,622 crore.
summary.overview: GSFC reported record Q4 FY26 sales of INR2,622 crore, with fertilizer sales of INR1,985 crore also a Q4 high. For FY26, standalone sales grew 15% to INR10,827 crore, operating EBITDA rose 24% to INR781 crore, and PAT rose 14% to INR652 crore. The Industrial Products segment posted its highest annual profit in four years (INR200 crore) and its best Q4 EBIT in ten quarters, helped by HX Crystal, traded ammonia and melamine exports, though caprolactam and nylon realisations were under pressure. Management said Q1 FY27 faces unsettled raw material markets, and it is managing the fertilizer mix around sulphur and ammonia supply.

segments.name: Fertilizer
segments.commentary: FY26 fertilizer sales volume rose 12% to 22.31 lakh MT from 19.88 lakh MT, led by AS, APS and DAP; fertilizer production hit a five-year high of 17.59 lakh MT. Segment sales rose INR1,196 crore for the year.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Delivered highest annual profit of INR200 crore in four years and highest Q4 EBIT in ten quarters. Growth came from HX Crystal, traded ammonia and melamine exports, while caprolactam and nylon realisations were under pressure from lower global spreads.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 fertilizer: raw material markets unsettled; government NBS rate revision for H1 FY27 gives a 10% uplift across nitrogen, phosphorus and sulphur nutrients to support kharif supply.
Management said there will be no production shortfall in Q1 FY27 for fertilizers, with ammonium sulphate imports arriving in the current month.

Industrial products: caprolactam-benzene spreads expected to recover, but elevated caprolactam and nylon 6 prices of Q4 unlikely to hold; melamine and technical grade urea face softer demand; export volumes expected to hold.

Fertilizer margin: DAP and urea margins expected unchanged as they are protected by government; government special package for extra DAP costs expected via circular soon; NPK grades could move plus or minus 5-10%.
IP segment expected to offset any fertilizer margin loss; caprolactam-benzene spread was above $800/MT currently versus about $670/MT in Q4.
capex_capacity: Capitalised major growth projects worth over INR670 crore in FY26, per management.
Sikka DAP train (1,300-1,400 MT/day) being converted to produce APS or DAP; completion expected in July or August 2026.
Ammonia plants 3 and 4 running at 100%; ammonia stock around 16,000 MT at Baroda complex.
Sulphuric acid tanks at full inventory level, but sulphur supply under long-term contracts (Reliance, Nayara, BPCL, IOCL) is not 100%, so imports are being sought.
demand_pricing: Fertilizer demand described as robust, supported by higher subsidy support; company running at optimum fertilizer utilisation with ammonium sulphate output at maximum possible given sulphur constraints.
Sulphur international price cited at about $850/MT; natural gas prices controlled by government, with increases absorbed through subsidy.
Melamine and technical grade urea demand soft; HX Crystal domestic demand constant; agrochemical sector absorbing geopolitical knock-on effects.
Government subsidy dues received for urea up to fourth week of April 2026 and P&K up to third week of April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How is the organisation positioned for FY27 given geopolitical disruption and import dependence, and what consistent numbers should investors expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the situation abnormal with raw material prices up manifold. Ammonia is made from domestically supplied gas at Fertilizer Nagar, where gas prices are government-controlled and absorbed via subsidy; sulphuric acid stock is sufficient for Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory position and replenishment pipeline for raw materials?
qa_highlights.answer: Ammonia stock about 16,000 MT at Baroda with 100% plant run rates; sulphuric acid tanks full. Sulphur supply under long-term contracts is partial and expensive, so spot imports are being arranged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company continuing ammonia trading?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Ammonia is imported through the company's own Sikka jetty and storage, with volumes for industry sold and ammonia traded from Jamnagar.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the fertilizer plant changeover to produce alternative grades, and what is the outlook for each segment?
qa_highlights.answer: One DAP train at Sikka (1,300-1,400 MT/day) is being converted to produce APS or DAP; completion expected July or August 2026. Fertilizer running at optimum levels; IP spreads improved to over $800/MT from about $670/MT.

qa_highlights.question: What fertilizer per-ton margin and blended volume should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a precise margin given volatility. DAP and urea margins are unchanged due to government protection; NPK grades may vary by plus or minus 5-10%, offset by IP segment performance.

risks_watch: Sulphur and ammonia supply constraints and high import prices; sulphur supply not at 100% of contract volumes.
Government special package for DAP cost reimbursement not yet issued; margin protection depends on the circular.
Caprolactam and nylon 6 prices expected to fall from Q4 peaks; melamine and technical urea demand soft.
Monsoon progress and possible El Nino affecting kharif demand.
Subsidy receivable timing: urea and P&K dues cleared only to late April 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and the IP turnaround, but cautious and somewhat evasive on forward fertilizer margins and raw material costs, which management said are too volatile to quantify. Stable operations and government backing were stressed more than specific FY27 targets.
key_quotes: So whatever margin loss we will be having in the fertilizer will be compensated by the IP product segment as I told that it is shaping up very nicely the prices of the chemical side.
We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with no long-term debt, healthy net worth and adequate liquidity.
So there will not be any production deficiency in the current quarter.
